iridoline: A nitrogenous base C10H9N, extracted from coal-tar naphtha, as an oily liquid. It is a member of the quinoline series, and is probably identical with lepidine.
ironbarktree: The Australian Eucalyptus Sideroxylon, used largely by carpenters and shipbuilders; -- called also ironwood.

irrecognition: A failure to recognize; absence of recognition. Lamb.
irresponsive: Not responsive; not able, ready, or inclined to respond.
irradiate: 1. To throw rays of light upon; to illuminate; to brighten; to adorn with luster. Thy smile irradiates yon blue fields. Sir W. Jones. 2. To enlighten intellectually; to illuminate; | Illuminated; irradiated. Mason.
irate: Angry; incensed; enraged. [Recent] The irate colonel . . . stood speechless. Thackeray. Mr. Jaggers suddenly became most irate. Dickens.
ironwort: An herb of the Mint family (Sideritis), supposed to heal sword cuts; also, a species of Galeopsis.
irpe: A fantastic grimace or contortion of the body. (old) Smirks and irps and all affected humors. B. Jonson .
ironmaster: A manufacturer of iron, or large dealer therein. Bp. Hurd.
irresuscitable: Incapable of being resuscitated or revived. -- Ir`re*sus"ci*ta*bly, adv.
irregular: Not regular; not conforming to a law, method, or usage recognized as the general rule; not according to common form; not conformable to nature, to the rules of moral rectitude, or to established… | One who is not regular; especially, a soldier not in regular service.
irisdiaphragm: An adjustable diaphragm, suggesting the iris of the eye in its action, for regulating the aperture of a lens, consisting of a number of thin pieces fastened to a ring. It is used in cameras and microscopes.
iridosmine: The native compound of iridium and osmium. It is found in flattened metallic grains of extreme hardness, and is often used for pointing gold pens.
irrigation: The act or process of irrigating, or the state of being irrigated; especially, the operation of causing water to flow over lands, for nourishing plants.
irrevocable: Incapable of being recalled or revoked; unchangeable; irreversible; unalterable; as, an irrevocable promise or decree; irrevocable fate. Firm and irrevocable is my doom. Shak. -- Ir*rev"o*ca*ble*ness, n. -- Ir*rev"o*ca*bly, adv.
irreligiousness: The state or quality of being irreligious; ungodliness.
irrelation: The quality or state of being irrelative; want of connection or relation.
irrepressibly: In a manner or to a degree that can not be repressed.
irresistible: That can not be successfully resisted or opposed; superior to opposition; resistless; overpowering; as, an irresistible attraction. An irresistible law of our nature impels us to seek happiness. J. M. Mason.
irisated: Exhibiting the prismatic colors; irised; iridescent. W. Phillips.
irp: A fantastic grimace or contortion of the body. (old) Smirks and irps and all affected humors. B. Jonson .
irritation: 1. irrefragability: The quality or state of being irrefragable; incapability of being refuted.
irregulate: To make irregular; to disorder. (old) Sir T. Browne.
iridian: Of or pertaining to the iris or rainbow.
irremovable: Not removable; immovable; inflexible. Shak. -- Ir`re*mov"a*bly, adv.

irreducibility: The state or quality of being irreducible.
iridescent: Having colors like the rainbow; exhibiting a play of changeable colors; nacreous; prismatic; as, iridescent glass.

iridectomy: The act or process of cutting out a portion of the iris in order to form an artificial pupil.
irreconcilability: The quality or state of being irreconcilable; irreconcilableness.
irritant: Rendering null and void; conditionally invalidating. The states elected Harry, Duke of Anjou, for their king, with this clause irritant; that, if he did violate any part of his oath, the people… | Irritating; producing irritation or inflammation.
irrevoluble: That has no finite period of revolution; not revolving. The dateless and irrevocable circle of eternity. Milton.
ironbound: 1. Bound as with iron; rugged; as, an ironbound coast. 2. Rigid; unyielding; as, ironbound traditions.
irish: Of or pertaining to Ireland or to its inhabitants; produced in Ireland. Irish elk. (Zoöl.) See under Elk. -- Irish moss. (a) (Bot.) Carrageen. (b) A preparation of the same made into a blanc mange. | 1. pl. The natives or inhabitants of Ireland, esp. the Celtic natives or their descendants. 2. ir: . A form of the prefix in-. See In-.
irrepresentable: Not capable of being represented or portrayed.
ironstone: A hard, earthy ore of iron. Clay ironstone. See under Clay. -- Ironstone china, a hard white pottery, first made in England during the 18th century.
irrespectively: Without regard to conditions; not making circumstances into consideration. Prosperity, considered absolutely and irrespectively, is better and more desirable than adversity. South.
irradiance: 1. The act of irradiating; emission of rays of light. 2. That which irradiates or is irradiated; luster; splendor; irradiation; brilliancy. Milton.
irrubrical: Contrary to the rubric; not rubrical.
irrefrangible: Not refrangible; that can not be refracted in passing from one medium to another. -- Ir`re*fran"gi*ble*ness, n.
irreligion: The state of being irreligious; want of religion; impiety.
irresolution: Want of resolution; want of decision in purpose; a fluctuation of mind, as in doubt, or between hope and fear; irresoluteness; indecision; vacillation. irretraceable: Incapable of being retraced; not retraceable.
irenic: Fitted or designed to promote peace; pacific; conciliatory; peaceful. Bp. Hall.
irreprovable: Incapable of being justly reproved; irreproachable; blameless; upright. -- Ir`re*prov"a*ble*ness, n. -- Ir`re*prov"a*bly, adv.
irresilient: Not resilient; not recoiling or rebounding; inelastic.
irriguous: 1. Watered; watery; moist; dewy. (old) The flowery lap Of some irriguous valley spreads her store. Milton. 2. Gently penetrating or pervading. (old) J. Philips.

ironware: Articles made of iron, as household utensils, tools, and the like.
irreverence: The state or quality of being irreverent; want of proper reverence; disregard of the authority and character of a superior.
irredeemability: The state or quality of being irredeemable; irredeemableness.
irreversibleness: The state or quality of being irreversible.
irrelapsable: Not liable to relapse; secure. Dr. H. More.
irresponsibility: Want of, or freedom from, responsibility or accountability.
irenarch: An officer in the Greek empire having functions corresponding to those of a justice of the peace. [Written also eirenarch.]
ironheads: A European composite herb (Centaurea nigra); -- so called from the resemblance of its knobbed head to an iron ball fixed on a long handle. Dr. Prior.
iridescence: Exhibition of colors like those of the rainbow; the quality or state of being iridescent; a prismatic play of color; as, the iridescence of mother-of-pearl.

irreconcilement: The state or quality of being unreconciled; disagreement.
irongray: Of a gray color, somewhat resembling that of iron freshly broken. -- n. An iron-gray color; also, a horse of this color.
ironmonger: A dealer in iron or hardware.

irrelavancy: The quality or state of being irrelevant; as, the irrelevancy of an argument.

irreverend: Irreverent. (old) Immodest speech, or irreverend gesture. Strype.
irroration: The act of bedewing; the state of being moistened with de (old) Chambers.

irremediableness: The state or quality of being irremediable.

irishry: The Celtic people of Ireland. "The whole Irishry of rebels." Milton.

irenical: Fitted or designed to promote peace; pacific; conciliatory; peaceful. Bp. Hall.

irretrievableness: The state or quality of being irretrievable.

irreclaimable: Incapable of being reclaimed. Addison. -- Ir`re*claim"a*bly, ad

irregularity: The state or quality of being irregular; that which is irregular.

irremediable: Not to be remedied, corrected, or redressed; incurable; as, an irremediable disease or evil.
irian: Of or pertaining to the iris. "Irian nerves." Dunglison.

irreversibility: The state or quality of being irreversible; irreversibleness.

irreproachableness: The quality or state of being irreproachable; integrity; innocence.
irrepealability: The quality or state of being irrepealable.

irreconcile: To prevent from being reconciled; to alienate or disaffect. (old)
iranian: Of or pertaining to Iran. -- n. A native of Iran; also, the Iranian or Persian language, a division of the Aryan family of languages.
ire: Anger; wrath. [Poet.] Syn. -- Anger; passion; rage; fury. See Anger.

irretentive: Not retentive; as, an irretentive memory.
